_README: COPY THIS FILE TO identity.json AND FILL IN THE THREE VALUES FROM PARTNER CENTER.
identity.json is gitignored; this example is the committed one. The three values
are not secrets, but they are ACCOUNT-SPECIFIC and wrong values produce a package
the Store rejects at ingestion with a message about identity mismatch - so they
live in one uncommitted file instead of being pasted into a manifest by hand.
WHERE EACH ONE COMES FROM. Partner Center > your app > Product management >
Product identity. That page lists all three, ready to copy:
name                  -> 'Package/Identity/Name'
e.g. 12345NurIfranArpon.Spaceadom
publisher             -> 'Package/Identity/Publisher'
ALWAYS a full X.500 subject starting with CN=,
usually CN=<a GUID>. It must match the SIGNING
CERTIFICATE'S SUBJECT EXACTLY, character for
character -- that is what makes the local
self-signed test cert in build-msix.ps1 usable at
all, because the script derives the cert's subject
FROM this value rather than the other way round.
publisherDisplayName  -> 'Package/Properties/PublisherDisplayName'
The human-readable name shown to users.
Must be your Partner Center publisher display name.
The VERSION is NOT here. It is read from package.json by build-msix.ps1 and
written as a.b.c.0 -- the fourth field is reserved by the Store, which is why
there is nothing to configure and nothing to keep in step by hand.
The Store RE-SIGNS the package it distributes with a Microsoft-issued
certificate, so the self-signed cert this repo can make is for LOCAL
STRUCTURAL TESTING ONLY and never leaves the machine. (Widely documented;
not re-confirmed against a live Microsoft Learn URL on 2026-09-05 -- the page
the research pass tried had moved. Verify in Partner Center before relying on
it for anything that matters.)
